title: JANUS Engine — TOPA + Spider calcium-scale prevention, crystal management and washable-trap crawl
mission: identify practical CaCO3 antiscalants suitable for a low-mineral recirculating water loop
prefer chemistries that inhibit adhesion or keep precipitate soft/dispersed rather than creating hard wall scale
connect chemistry to removable washable side-stream filters / crystal traps
preserve membrane, PEMFC, seals and oxygen-side compatibility boundaries

archive_and_literature_result.internal_registry_search: No prior dedicated JANUS antiscalant record was found in the accessible meta-registry code search during this pass.

arxiv_anchor.title: Adsorption isotherm and mechanism of Ca2+ binding to polyelectrolyte
arxiv_anchor.relevance: supports sodium polyacrylate/PAA as a mechanistically grounded CaCO3 antiscalant candidate

industrial_review_2026.finding: phosphonates and polycarboxylates remain leading industrial inhibitor families; common representatives include PBTC, ATMP, HEDP and PAA, with many applications in roughly 1-10 mg/L ranges
industrial_review_2026.caution: mechanisms are more complex than simple calcium chelation; dosage must be validated against actual water chemistry

candidate_rank.why_JANUS: strong CaCO3 evidence, phosphorus-free, can reduce adherent scale and favor smaller/dispersed particles that are compatible with a side-stream washable trap concept
evidence: Desalination 268 (2011) 38-45 PAA inhibited CaCO3 and CaSO4 in cooling-water tests
Desalination 397 (2016) 43-52 polymer antiscalants inhibited calcite growth in recirculating cooling pilot plants
candidate_rank.JANUS_boundary: Must be tested for adsorption/fouling on the selected POMS support and for any effect on dissolved-O2 transport before full-loop dosing.

candidate_rank.candidate: polyaspartic acid (PASP), optionally studied with PESA
candidate_rank.why_JANUS: PASP has industrial-circuit CaCO3 growth-inhibition evidence; PASP/PESA mixtures have shown delayed nucleation plus strong growth suppression, offering a lower-phosphorus path
evidence: Water Research 186 (2020) 116334: PASP and PAA inhibited CaCO3 crystal growth; PESA delayed nucleation; PASP+PESA mixture produced long delay and strong inhibition in the tested circuit
candidate_rank.JANUS_boundary: Biodegradability can be environmentally attractive but may affect microbiological control in a warm closed loop; biofouling must be monitored.

candidate_rank.role: high-efficiency threshold inhibitor / crystal morphology modifier
candidate_rank.why_JANUS: very strong industrial CaCO3 scale-inhibition precedent and recent evidence that HEDP-4Na makes CaCO3 less ordered and less adherent
evidence: Journal of Crystal Growth 691 (2026) 128674: HEDP-4Na changed CaCO3 morphology and reduced adhesion
Desalination 631 (2026) 120221: HEDP/PBTC/ATMP remain widespread commercial inhibitors
candidate_rank.JANUS_boundary: Phosphonates can themselves form calcium/magnesium-phosphonate deposits under some conditions and add phosphorus to the water. Treat as secondary candidate until compatibility and speciation are measured.

candidate_rank.why_JANUS: well-established antiscalant performance and strong calcite-deposition reduction in comparative studies
evidence: 2022 calcite inhibitor comparison found SHMP highly effective against CaCO3 deposition
candidate_rank.JANUS_boundary: Polyphosphate hydrolysis/reversion, phosphorus loading and possible long-term chemistry drift make it less attractive than PAA/PASP for the first closed-loop JANUS trial.

candidate_rank.role: offline or condition-triggered descaling/cleaning, not preferred as continuous-dose primary inhibitor
candidate_rank.why_JANUS: membrane-industry cleaning guidance commonly uses citric acid for early carbonate-scale removal
candidate_rank.JANUS_boundary: Continuous acidification can alter corrosion, materials, membrane transport and system pH. Use only in an isolated cleaning cycle after material-compatibility validation.

strongest_architecture_connection.name: CALCIFER_SIDE_STREAM_CRYSTAL_TRAP
strongest_architecture_connection.principle: Do not rely on chemistry to keep all calcium dissolved forever. Use low-mineral make-up water + low-dose antiscalant to prevent wall adhesion, then route a small side-stream through a removable crystal-collection chamber.
strongest_architecture_connection.industrial_precedent: Fluidized-bed pellet softening intentionally crystallizes CaCO3 onto seed media and removes pellets. Such reactors have decades of water-softening precedent and power-plant circulating-water applications.
JANUS_adaptation: main Axle chamber stays near neutral operating chemistry and receives the inhibitor/dispersant only after compatibility validation
scraper/wiper action removes nascent wall scale before it becomes thick
centrifugal flow sends detached solids toward an outer gutter
side-stream washable basket/filter captures loose particles
optional future seed-crystal cassette provides a preferred nucleation surface so calcium deposits in a serviceable chamber instead of on the Axle or POMS stack
filter differential pressure or mass gain becomes a maintenance signal

mechanical_boundary.decision: Do not use rigid metal-to-wall rubbing as the default 'lathe' interface.
mechanical_boundary.preferred: controlled small radial clearance plus sacrificial/compliant scraper or wiper inserts carried by the Axle ring
mechanical_boundary.reason: direct hard contact risks wear debris, galling, heat, seal damage, rotor seizure and contamination of membrane/PEMFC water. The scraping edge should be replaceable and softer/engineered relative to the chamber wall.

measure: CaCO3 mass captured in washable trap
proposed_first_matrix.selection_metric: minimize adherent-wall CaCO3 and O2-flux loss while maximizing removable-trap capture at the lowest reagent dose and lowest parasitic burden

spider_verdict.green_candidate: PASP, with PASP+PESA as an exploratory synergistic pair
spider_verdict.best_system_level_move: combine low-dose anti-adhesion chemistry with mechanical Axle wiping plus a removable side-stream seed/filter trap
